answer: In this PoA design, an agent registers a public key only after a fresh, verifier-checked hardware quote binds that key to an approved MRENCLAVE, the enclave’s code measurement. The enclave protects the signing key, so copying a VM or software image cannot reproduce its hardware-backed attestation. Creating additional identities therefore requires access to additional genuine TEE hardware, not merely virtual-machine duplication; saffron, nadir, and vine are ordinary agent labels, not attestation evidence.
